Box.description:
Explicit geometry: origin top-left, +x right, +y down (spec section 7.3).

Fields keep their raw unit strings; `deckifyr.schema.units.parse_length`
converts them to EMUs during plan resolution, not here.

x.description: Distance from the slide's left edge, with an explicit unit.
x.title: X

y.description: Distance from the slide's top edge, with an explicit unit.
y.title: Y

width.description: Box width with an explicit unit.
width.title: Width

height.description: Box height with an explicit unit.
height.title: Height

Box.title: Box

BrandingFurniture.description:
An organization/department label. Unlike `status`/`page_number`
there's no `enabled` flag -- whether the `furniture.branding` block is
present at all *is* the toggle, matching spec section 7.8's own
example YAML. `text` is a literal string: general variable/expression
substitution (e.g. `{organization}`) is a separate, still-open design
question (spec section 21) that this does not preempt.

text.description: Literal label text, such as an organization or department name.
text.title: Text

BrandingFurniture.title: BrandingFurniture

ColorDerivation.description:
One `colors:` entry computed from another token/literal instead of
a hand-picked literal hex value. `base` may name a `colors:` token or
a literal hex value, the same "token or bare literal" convention
every other color-bearing field in `design.yaml` already uses.
Exactly one of `lighten`/`darken`/`saturate`/`desaturate`/`mix` must
be set; `weight` (0.0-1.0, default 0.5 when `mix` is set) is only
valid alongside `mix` -- it's the fraction of `mix`'s own color
blended in (0.0 = all `base`, 1.0 = all `mix`).

base.description: The color to start from: a `colors:` token or a literal hex value.
base.title: Base

lighten.description: Lighten the base by this amount (0.0-1.0).
lighten.title: Lighten

darken.description: Darken the base by this amount (0.0-1.0).
darken.title: Darken

saturate.description: Increase the base's saturation by this amount (0.0-1.0).
saturate.title: Saturate

desaturate.description: Decrease the base's saturation by this amount (0.0-1.0).
desaturate.title: Desaturate

mix.description: Blend in this color (token or hex) instead of adjusting lightness or saturation.
mix.title: Mix

weight.description: With `mix`: how much of the mixed color to blend in, from 0.0 (all base) to 1.0 (all mix).
weight.title: Weight

ColorDerivation.title: ColorDerivation

overflow.description: What to do when text does not fit its box: fail the build, shrink it, clip it, or let it continue.
overflow.title: Overflow

image_fit.description: How an image fills its box when no `fit` is set on the element.
image_fit.title: Image Fit

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees applied to elements that set none.
rotation.title: Rotation

footer_height.description: Height of a reportifyr footer box placed directly beneath its element.
footer_height.title: Footer Height

footer_style.description: `text_styles` name used for footers when the element sets no `style`; unset uses a small built-in style.
footer_style.title: Footer Style

table_style.description: `table_styles` name used by tables that set no `table_style`; unset keeps the default template look.
table_style.title: Table Style

body.description: Default font family for body text.
body.title: Body

monospace.description: Font family for code and other monospaced text.
monospace.title: Monospace

Furniture.description:
`design.yaml`'s `furniture` block (spec section 7.8). Every field
is optional and unset by default -- a `DesignDocument` with no
furniture configured expands into nothing extra at all.

status.description: Draft/final status marks; a build selects one placement via `status_indicator`.

Furniture.title: Furniture

Gradient.description:
A linear gradient fill, usable anywhere a plain color fill is
(`SlideSize.background_gradient`, a `ShapeStyle.fill`). `angle`
follows `python-pptx`'s own `FillFormat.gradient_angle` convention:
0 is left-to-right, increasing angles rotate clockwise, so 90 (the
default) is top-to-bottom -- not the CSS `linear-gradient()`
convention some authors may expect from other tools.

stops.description: Color stops along the gradient path (at least 2).
stops.title: Stops

angle.description: Direction in degrees: 0 runs left to right and 90 (the default) top to bottom, increasing clockwise.
angle.title: Angle

Gradient.title: Gradient

GradientStop.description:
One color/position pair along a `Gradient`'s path -- mirrors
`python-pptx`'s own `a:gs` element, spec section 7.4's "token or bare
literal" convention for `color` included: `color` may name a
`design.yaml` `colors:` token or a literal hex value, resolved the
same way `TextStyle.color`/`ShapeStyle.fill` already are.

color.description: Stop color: a `colors:` token name or a literal hex value.
color.title: Color

position.description: Where along the gradient this stop sits, from 0.0 (start) to 1.0 (end).
position.title: Position

GradientStop.title: GradientStop

PageNumberFurniture.description:
A running page number. `format` supports exactly two placeholders,
`{page}` (1-indexed slide position) and `{total}` (slide count) --
a closed-form substitution the author cannot hand-write, not a
general templating mechanism (spec section 21's still-open decision
about broader variable/expression support is unrelated to this).

enabled.description: Show the page number on every slide.
enabled.title: Enabled

format.description: Text pattern; `{page}` is the 1-indexed slide number and `{total}` the slide count.
format.title: Format

box.description: Where the page number is drawn.

PageNumberFurniture.title: PageNumberFurniture

ShapeStyle.description:
A named fill/line style for `shape` elements, alongside `text_styles`
(spec section 7.4's planned "shape styles" -- see the `design.yaml`
table in spec section 7.2). Every field is optional and falls back to
`deckifyr.pptx.compose`'s own default (a thin black outline, no fill)
when unset, the same "token or bare literal" convention `TextStyle`'s
`font`/`color` fields use.

fill.description: Fill: a color token or hex value, or a gradient. Unset leaves the shape unfilled.
fill.title: Fill

line_color.description: Outline color: a `colors:` token name or a literal hex value.
line_color.title: Line Color

line_width.description: Outline thickness with an explicit unit, e.g. `1pt`.
line_width.title: Line Width

ShapeStyle.title: ShapeStyle

width.description: Slide width with an explicit unit, e.g. `13.333in`.
width.title: Width

height.description: Slide height with an explicit unit, e.g. `7.5in`.
height.title: Height

background.description: Solid slide background color; also the fallback behind a non-covering image or gradient.
background.title: Background

safe_area.description: Inset kept clear of content on every slide edge.
safe_area.title: Safe Area

background_image.description: Optional project-relative image painted behind all slide content.
background_image.title: Background Image

background_gradient.description: Optional gradient painted as the slide's native background fill, in front of `background`.

StatusFurniture.description:
A draft/final/status marker (spec section 7.8) -- off by default
(every field below is independently optional, and
`PresentationDocument.status_indicator` defaults to `None`/`"none"`),
flipped on for a specific build via `presentation.yaml` rather than
baked into `design.yaml` as always-on.

Each field is one placement `presentation.yaml`'s own
`status_indicator` may select -- a full, diagonal, page-spanning
watermark, or a small label in one of the slide's four corners --
with its own box/style/rotation/z_index (`StatusIndicatorStyle`).
`design.yaml` only has to configure the placements a project
actually intends to use; selecting one `status_indicator` has no
design-level style for it is a build-time
`ContentValidationError` (`deckifyr.plan._furniture_layout`), not a
silent no-op -- spec section 20 warning 7's "do not silently drop
content" applies here as much as anywhere else. Field names are
underscored (`corner_tr`, not `corner-tr`) to stay valid Python
identifiers; `StatusIndicatorMode`'s own literal values (what
`presentation.yaml` actually types) keep the hyphenated spelling,
since a YAML string has no such restriction.

corner_tr.description: Small label in the top-right corner.

corner_tl.description: Small label in the top-left corner.

corner_bl.description: Small label in the bottom-left corner.

corner_br.description: Small label in the bottom-right corner.

StatusFurniture.title: StatusFurniture

StatusIndicatorStyle.description:
One `status_indicator` placement's own appearance -- a status/
watermark mark has no content of its own (spec section 7.8's
`furniture.status` never carries a default word the way, say,
`branding.text` does): `presentation.yaml`'s own
`PresentationDocument.watermark` supplies the actual text, any build
may choose, and this only says where/how it's drawn once chosen.

`z_index` (unset by default) is what actually chooses which of the
two conventional "status mark" designs this is: left unset, it keeps
every other furniture item's own default
(`_FURNITURE_OVERLAY_Z_INDEX`, well behind ordinary content) -- the
right choice for a small, simple corner label (a `corner_*` field
below). Set to a large positive value, it paints on top of every
ordinary element instead -- a real diagonal watermark (Word/Google
Docs style) needs to read on top of whatever content it crosses, not
hide behind it, which is also why that use case should pair
`rotation` with a low `opacity` on its `style` (`TextStyle.opacity`)
rather than relying on placement alone.

box.description: Where the mark is drawn. A rotated mark pivots around the centre of this box.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees, e.g. -30 for a diagonal watermark.
rotation.title: Rotation

z_index.description: Stacking order. Unset paints behind content; a large positive value paints on top, like a watermark.
z_index.title: Z Index

StatusIndicatorStyle.title: StatusIndicatorStyle

TableStyle.description:
A named fill/border style for `table` elements, alongside
`shape_styles`. Every field is optional and, when unset, leaves
`python-pptx`'s own default table-template look (banding, header
fill, no explicit border) untouched for that aspect -- the same
"no style token = compositor's own built-in default" convention
`ShapeStyle` uses. Font/size/bold/italic and the body text color
remain governed by `text_styles` via a table element's ordinary
`style` field (unchanged); `TableStyle` only controls the fill/
border chrome `text_styles` has no vocabulary for. `header_fill`
overrides the default template's own header band; pair it with
`header_text_color` when the new fill would leave the template's
own (unshown, theme-inherited) header text color illegible --
`deckifyr.pptx.compose` does not infer one from the other.

header_fill.description: Fill color of the header row; unset keeps the default table template look.
header_fill.title: Header Fill

header_text_color.description: Header text color; set it alongside `header_fill` when the new fill would hide the default text.
header_text_color.title: Header Text Color

band_fill.description: Alternate-row fill for banding; unset means every body row uses `body_fill`.
band_fill.title: Band Fill

border_width.description: Cell border thickness with an explicit unit, e.g. `0.5pt`.
border_width.title: Border Width

TableStyle.title: TableStyle

font.description: Font family name, or a `fonts:` token such as `body`.
font.title: Font

size.description: Font size with an explicit unit, e.g. `18pt`.
size.title: Size

color.description: Text color: a `colors:` token name or a literal hex value.
color.title: Color

opacity.description: Text opacity from 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0 (opaque, the default when unset); mainly for watermark-style marks.
opacity.title: Opacity

text_transform.description: Case transform applied when the text is rendered; unset leaves it exactly as authored.
text_transform.title: Text Transform

fonts.description: Font families used by text styles.

colors.description: Named color tokens: a literal hex value, or a color derived from another token.
colors.title: Colors

text_styles.description: Named text styles that elements reference through `style`.
text_styles.title: Text Styles

defaults.description: Project-wide fallbacks for settings an element leaves unset.

furniture.description: Per-slide extras such as the status mark, branding label and page number.
